title: Give One Kinase an ATP of Its Own

scenes.tts: What if you have a kinase but do not know the substrates? The approaches each have a weakness. A purified kinase in a test tube shows what it can phosphorylate, which is more than it does in a cell. Prediction from sequence gives candidates.
scenes.visual: A kinase chip with three question-mark boxes; then a test tube panel where every protein gets a phosphate badge beside a cell panel where fewer do (idealised); then a sequence chip leading to dashed candidate chips.
scenes.narration: What if you have a kinase but do not know the substrates? The approaches each have a weakness. A purified kinase in a test tube shows what it can phosphorylate, which is more than it does in a cell. Prediction from sequence gives candidates.

scenes.tts: Finding the kinase bound to a protein shows contact, which is not catalysis. Removing the kinase with an inhibitor, R N A interference or a knockout changes many proteins. The direct substrates look the same as those three steps downstream.
scenes.caption: Finding the kinase bound to a protein shows contact, which is not catalysis. Removing the kinase with an inhibitor, RNA interference or a knockout changes many proteins. The direct substrates look the same as those three steps downstream.
scenes.visual: A kinase touches a protein, a question mark where a phosphate would be; then a chain kinase, A, B, C, D (for example): the kinase is crossed out and every chain protein is marked changed, the direct substrate and the one three steps downstream looking alike.
scenes.narration: Finding the kinase bound to a protein shows contact, which is not catalysis. Removing the kinase with an inhibitor, RNA interference or a knockout changes many proteins. The direct substrates look the same as those three steps downstream.

scenes.tts: Kevan Shokat's laboratory found a way through, which Professor Deppmann introduces as organic chemistry meets protein manipulation. Kinases share an A T P pocket. One bulky residue in it, the gatekeeper, limits what fits. Replace the gatekeeper with glycine or alanine, and the pocket gains a hole.
scenes.caption: Kevan Shokat's laboratory found a way through, which Professor Deppmann introduces as organic chemistry meets protein manipulation. Kinases share an ATP pocket. One bulky residue in it, the gatekeeper, limits what fits. Replace the gatekeeper with glycine or alanine, and the pocket gains a hole.
scenes.visual: A kinase block with a notch for the pocket; an orange gatekeeper block narrows it and ATP just fits; the gatekeeper is replaced by a small residue and a dashed hole appears.
scenes.narration: Kevan Shokat's laboratory found a way through, which Professor Deppmann introduces as organic chemistry meets protein manipulation. Kinases share an ATP pocket. One bulky residue in it, the gatekeeper, limits what fits. Replace the gatekeeper with glycine or alanine, and the pocket gains a hole.

scenes.tts: An A T P with a bulky group added to its adenine fits the enlarged pocket, and fits normal kinases poorly. Such a kinase is called analog-sensitive. The laboratory introduced the approach in 1997 with the tyrosine kinase vee Sark.
scenes.caption: An ATP with a bulky group added to its adenine fits the enlarged pocket, and fits normal kinases poorly. Such a kinase is called analog-sensitive. The laboratory introduced the approach in 1997 with the tyrosine kinase v-Src.
scenes.visual: An ATP carrying a purple bulky block seats in the enlarged pocket but stops short at a normal kinase's gatekeeper; the enlarged kinase is labelled analog-sensitive; 1997 and v-Src appear.
scenes.narration: An ATP with a bulky group added to its adenine fits the enlarged pocket, and fits normal kinases poorly. Such a kinase is called analog-sensitive. The laboratory introduced the approach in 1997 with the tyrosine kinase v-Src.
